defaults: Baselines are each cell's own pre-window, per sample / per request (decision round 4: ledger spread per request); the sensor_rep window rule (no-fault tiles, window medians) is not used for timing because a window median has no time.

K = 4, scale 1.4826, floors from sensor_rep/catch.py (span latency 1 ms, ledger 1 ms, metric floors from symptoms.py / lmt_detect.py, else 2 % of the median); comparator `>=`; >= 3 pre-window samples for a level threshold.

run3 = 3 consecutive samples; median = online median of >= 3 in-window samples; absent = silence > 2 x the longest pre-window gap after >= 5 pre-window records. One rule pool for every channel; no detector selection (§2b not run).

No-fault windows: hold-length windows at onset_med + i·hold inside every valid no-fault cell of the posture, each with its own pre-window; windows of one cell are not independent (n_eff is stated with its cells). Later windows have longer pre-windows than the fault cells.

G3 per (posture, sensor, rule) at τ = 0.05. Hotel n_eff = 20 per posture (k <= 1 admissible); TeaStore and OTel 6 (k = 0). TeaStore no-fault cells hold no application log records, so log rules there cannot be removed by G3.
The affected call path for spikes is service-level (target, transitive callers, transitive callees in the project map's call graph); per-request trace attribution was not done.
Observation time = when a record becomes available (span end, request end, log stamp, metric stamp). docker stats and cgroup rates are stamped at the end of their interval.
Detection is counted only inside the hold [command bound, hold end]; a catch after the revert is not a detection.
Ledger readers: visibility.hotel_ledger_rows / teastore_ledger_rows (checked equal, journey index kept) / otel_ledger_rows. Ledger latency baselines are per route; TeaStore has four routes.
OTel: barrier-relative fault offsets against the ledger's own start stamp (taken after the barrier), skew not measured.
Thinning keeps the full-rate admissible ledger rules; E only (failed, spike, run3, median).
findings: **The ledger's time to detection on a stopping fault is the client timeout plus the wait for the first request on the path.** Hotel pauses: E 16/16 in every population, 1.13-1.18 s from the command bound (client timeout 1 s; the first affected request starts 0.16 s after the command, median). TeaStore: 15.17-15.30 s (auth-freeze, 9/9) and 16.30-18.00 s (persistence-crash, 9/9; 15 s timeout). OTel: 15.67-15.74 s in 11/12, 6.70 s in 1 (15 s timeout; the ledger is the target's own sensor there, because the target is the entry). Every one of these catches is the `failed` rule and every one carries BC-ledger-stopped-on-path.

**A per-request latency rule is G3-inadmissible everywhere it was tested.** `spike` (one request beyond median + max(4·1.4826·MAD, 1 ms) of its route's pre-window) and `watchdog` (an in-flight request's age crossing that threshold) fire in 7-20 of 20 Hotel no-fault windows per posture, 5-6 of 6 TeaStore, 2-3 of 6 OTel: 0 of 15 (population, posture) cells admissible. `failed`, `run3` and `median` have 0 no-fault firings in all 15. The watchdog would have caught the Hotel pauses at 0.14-0.19 s instead of ~1.16 s; it is excluded by G3, not by choice. Rule set: engineering default of this analysis (decision round 4 fixed per-request spread, not the rule's aggregation).

**Where a sensor is faster than the ledger at full load, it is by construction or a tracer copy of the ledger; Hotel's logs are not resolvably faster at all.** Hotel reservation-pause: frontend's error log `SearchHandler CheckAvailability failed` (BC-caller-log) catches 12/12 in lmt2 and in sel1 (int1 has no reservation fault). Its stamps are whole seconds, so each catch is an interval [s, s + 1) − onset: of the 26 Hotel log catches (24 reservation-pause, 2 search-pause), 24 intervals contain the ledger's time and 2 lie wholly after it; none lies wholly before it, and none is stamped in the onset second. At the conservative end (s + 1, used in every table) the log is slower than the ledger in all 26: per-posture medians 1.49-1.94 s vs E 1.16-1.17 s. A first version of this document timed logs at the stamp itself (0.49-0.94 s) and called them faster; that was withdrawn after a parallel check by the main session. Without BC no log catch remains (0/12). Hotel pauses, M: callers' and the delayed path's CPU dropping (BC-idle-cpu), per-posture medians 1.48-1.50 s in 8 of 10 (class, posture) cells and 7.63-7.64 s in 2; 0/8-0/12 without BC. Without BC, the remaining span catch of every Hotel pause is the entry's own root span erroring (`span:frontend:HTTP_GET_/hotels:error`, 1.16 s, the same instant as the ledger); the MAP taxonomy does not flag it, and whether it should is the user's call. TeaStore persistence-crash (sub-second log stamps): auth's warning (BC-caller-log) 9/9 at 13.38-13.41 s vs E 16.30-18.00 s, the only log catches wholly ahead of the ledger; without BC only `full`'s webui LoginActionServlet latency spike remains, 3/3 at 13.41-13.43 s.

**BC-caller-log is structural here and over-reaches in 3 episodes.** It flags a warn/error template of a direct caller of the target. Of 36 flagged (template, episode) pairs, 33 carry a message about the call to the target (`SearchHandler CheckAvailability failed` during reservation-pause, 24; auth's exception-mapper warning during persistence-crash, 9; listing below). The other 3 are frontend logs about a different callee: `GetProfiles failed` (sel1 reservation-pause, int1 search-pause) and `CheckAvailability failed` (sel1 search-pause). A content rule would leave those 3 unflagged; two of them are the 1/12 L catches of search-pause (stamp intervals [14.72, 15.72] and [14.56, 15.56] s, ending after the 15.0 s hold).

**The delays are where spans beat a ledger that misses.** hotel-int1 (2 ms delay): geo-delay E 4/4, 4/4, 2/4, 0/4 under none, metrics, selected, full, while search's client span to geo catches 4/4 under selected (0.31 s median) and full (0.06 s); rate-delay E 4/4, 4/4, 2/4, 1/4, spans 4/4 at 0.26 s and 0.20 s. This is the posture-dependent ledger threshold of decision 9, now in time. lmt2/sel1 net-delay (larger, ~200 ms): E 16/16 at 0.43-0.57 s (run3/median), T/Tsel 4/4 at 0.36-0.46 s. These span catches are not BC-flagged because the taxonomy flags caller spans only for stopping faults; they time the target's RPC.

**The cgroup sampler (S, 5 s) is at its false-alarm rate in a 15 s hold.** Its catches fall on the sample instants (4.8, 9.8, 14.8 s after the bound) and its leave-one-cell-out family false-alarm rate in no-fault windows reaches 9/20 (hotel-sel1 none). Most S catches are `sys_memory`. The one recurring pattern beyond that is frontend's memory rising while search is paused (`spike`, mostly at the first sample after the bound, 4.86-4.87 s; the first no-BC S catch in 4/16 lmt2, 6/16 sel1, 7/16 int1 search-pause episodes; not BC-flagged). The cpu-throttle is caught by no outside family clearly above its false-alarm rate (E 0/16 in every population; S 3/16, 6/16, 6/16 in lmt2, sel1, int1, mostly at 14.8 s, against family false-alarm rates of 0-7/20 per posture); the throttled service's own PSI catches 11-15 of 16 at 4.67-9.81 s (G2: own).

**Impact before detection** (ledger requests started between the bound and the first catch that failed or crossed their route's per-request threshold; detected episodes): Hotel pauses E 11 (every episode), caller log L 11-20 (timed at the stamp's end; median 15 and 16 in lmt2 and sel1), docker CPU M 14-75; TeaStore auth-freeze E 3, persistence-crash E 1-2 of 26 bad in the hold; OTel E:own 7-8. Under the per-request threshold almost every hold request of a Hotel pause is bad (149 of 150), so the count is the rate times the time to detection.

**Thinning the ledger (a bound on the ledger side only): on Hotel pauses** the ledger's miss share within the 15 s hold is 0.00 down to 1 req/s, 0.05-0.06 at 0.2, 0.24-0.25 at 0.1 and 0.86-0.87 at 0.01 req/s (Bernoulli, 200 seeds × 16 episodes); the Poisson prediction exp(-r q (H - d - l)) gives 0.08, 0.27, 0.88. Mean time to detection with misses charged at the hold end (decision 15): 1.16 s at 10 req/s, 2.04-2.08 at 1, 5.66-5.82 at 0.2, 8.56-8.75 at 0.1, 13.97-14.10 at 0.01. A periodic schedule at the same rates never misses down to 0.1 req/s (one request every 10 s always lands in a 15 s hold). OTel (1 req/s base): miss 0.20 at 0.02 req/s, 0.44 at 0.01. Thinned latency rules re-estimate their baseline from few requests and false-alarm (TeaStore 171/3600 no-fault windows at p = 0.2); the failure rule alone has 0 false alarms at every rate.

**Crossover.** On Hotel pauses, docker CPU (M) is faster than the thinned ledger in more than half the trials from 1 req/s down in 3 of 5 (population, pause class) cells and from 0.5 and 0.2 req/s in the other two (analytic 2.26-2.32 req/s; 0.115 for lmt2 reservation-pause, whose M median is 7.6 s), and the caller log (timed at its stamp's end) from 1 req/s down (analytic 1.71 and 1.38 req/s); without BC neither has a catch (0/8, 0/12). The caller log is emitted per failed call, so it thins with the requests too: its row is not a request-independent comparison. The S family on int1 search-pause (9/16, mostly frontend memory) is faster from 0.01 req/s. On cpu-throttle any catch beats a ledger that never catches. **Every one of these signals plausibly needs load** (idle callers, per-call error logs, blocked requests holding memory, CPU demand under a quota); thinning cannot show that, so the crossover rates are where the ledger would lose if the sensor's signal did not weaken with load. That is the question decision 15's traffic sweep has to answer on the host.

Scope of every line above: **instance** (one host and one campaign per population; n = 4 episodes per Hotel (class, posture), 3 per TeaStore and OTel; no-fault windows are sub-windows of 4 or 3 cells). The rules are this analysis's engineering defaults; under the window rule of `research/protocol/sensor_rep/` the detection counts differ (e.g. its ledger 16/16 on the int1 delays).
